en: Xi'an in Two, Three or Five Days
zh: 西安两日、三日与五日行程
ja: 西安を巡る二日、三日、五日

p.src: At the Small Wild Goose Pagoda in the morning, resist adding the next stop immediately. The tower narrows as it rises; close-set eaves cast thin shadows, and the top ends abruptly. Those details need a little time at close range. The four guides stop on the stone path, open their route notebook and keep only one morning group: the pagoda, the Jianfu Temple precinct and Xi'an Museum. A Xi'an day should not be measured by how many famous places it contains. A better measure is whether the traveler stays in one part of the city, has time to understand one place, eats properly, rests, and returns to the hotel without a scramble.

caption.zh: 在小雁塔前，先留时间看塔身层层收分、密檐与不完整的顶部，再决定上午是否还需要下一处。四位向导只保留小雁塔、荐福寺院落与西安博物院这一组。
caption.ja: 小雁塔では、上へ細くなる塔身、密な軒、途中で切れた頂部を見る時間を先に取る。四人が午前に残したのは、小雁塔、薦福寺の境内、西安博物院という一組だけである。
caption.en: At the Small Wild Goose Pagoda, leave time for the taper, close-set eaves and broken top before deciding whether the morning needs another place. The four guides keep only the pagoda, Jianfu Temple precinct and Xi'an Museum as one group.

p.src: These are not three unrelated itineraries. They are one route built by adding coherent days. With two days, keep Day 1 inside the old core and give Day 2 to Qin archaeology in Lintong. A third day adds one museum and one pagoda in the south. With five days, Day 4 chooses one nearby place, while Day 5 stays in the city to recover a missed stop or follow one new subject in depth. Lines on the map show editorial order and relative position only. They do not describe walking, metro, road geometry, journey time or a shuttle operating on the travel date.

caption.zh: 两日行程是第一、二天；三日再加城南；五日再加一处近郊和一天市内余量。第四天的四处只选一处。连线表示先后和方位，不是步行、铁路、公路、车程或实时导航。
caption.ja: 二日なら一・二日目、三日なら市南部を追加し、五日なら近郊一か所と市内の余白を足す。四日目の候補は一か所だけ選ぶ。線は順序と方角で、徒歩、鉄道、道路、所要時間、当日のナビではない。
caption.en: Two days use Days 1-2; three adds the southern corridor; five adds one nearby place and a city-depth day. Choose only one Day 4 option. Lines show order and position, not walking, rail, road, journey time or live navigation.

p.src: Before building a day, write five lines: its geography; the one place that needs a reservation or the most energy; the neighboring sequence that follows naturally; one meal eaten sitting down; and the margin for rest and return. If those five items will not fit, the problem is usually the day, not the paper. Put the fixed entry near the centre of the plan. Keep the morning in the same area as the booked place and allow only one afternoon extension. After dinner, do not cross the city merely to add another name. This method does not show less of Xi'an. It lets the wall, the pits, a pagoda and a bowl of noodles be experienced separately.

p.src: Keep Day 1 within and immediately beside the Ming wall. Begin at Yongning Gate to establish direction. Walk one wall section, then come down; do not make a complete circuit the goal. Continue through Shuyuanmen toward Beilin. Enter the museum only if stone inscriptions and calligraphy matter to you and enough museum time remains. After a late arrival, keep Shuyuanmen and move Beilin to Day 5. In the afternoon, continue to Bell and Drum Tower, then the Great Mosque in Huajue Lane and the surrounding streets. Enter worship space quietly under the rules on site and ask before photographing. Choose one seated dinner for noodles or paomo instead of replacing the evening with a succession of snacks. The point is not to finish the wall. It is to see how gates, towers, a mosque and lived-in lanes occupy the same old core.

p.src: On Day 2, fix the Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum Museum entry first, then work backward to wake-up, breakfast and hotel departure. In Lintong, do not spend all your attention on the first ranks in Pit 1. Read the pit structure, partitions and conservation areas, then follow the contrast among Pits 1, 2 and 3: the broad formation, mixed units, and the much smaller space whose function remains debated. If energy and current museum operations allow, continue to Lishan Garden to see how the burial mound and accompanying pits relate to the warrior pits and the wider mausoleum. Huaqing Palace is not an automatic addition. Include it only when it was always the day's second subject and current admission and return arrangements still work. The return, security, local transfer and a meal belong to the day; they are not empty space on the map.

p.src: Keep Day 3 in the south and choose one museum with enough substance for the morning. If Shaanxi History Museum is booked, enter at the real-name time slot and begin with the basic display rather than chasing every temporary exhibition. Its three halls and seven chronological sections range from prehistoric Shaanxi into later history, with especially strong Zhou, Qin, Han and Tang material. This is where the city and mausoleum seen on the first two days can share one timeline. Eat lunch and sit for a while before continuing to the Big Wild Goose Pagoda and Da Ci'en Temple. At the tower, the relationship among Xuanzang, translation and Tang Chang'an will mean more than another hurried dynasty list in a gallery. Spend the evening around Yanta, eat there, and return to the hotel instead of crossing back to Bell Tower for an extra sight.

p.src: Failing to secure Shaanxi History Museum does not ruin Day 3. Replace the entire morning with the Small Wild Goose Pagoda, the Jianfu Temple precinct and Xi'an Museum. That remains a complete route: examine the close-eaved brick tower and its broken top in the garden, then use the museum for city archaeology and local objects. Only after lunch decide whether to continue to the Big Wild Goose Pagoda. The two Wild Goose Pagodas are different buildings; there is no need to race between them simply to complete a pair. If access to the Small Pagoda group also changes, choose one verified open museum and remove the original plan. Do not stack the fallback on top. Recheck each reservation, entrance and opening status before leaving.

p.src: The four names on the Day 4 map do not form a route. Huashan suits a traveler able to give the day to weather, transfers, cableway or mountain walking. Han Yangling continues the archaeology thread but moves attention from Qin military formations to a Han imperial burial landscape, accompanying pits and objects of ordinary life. Cuihuashan is a managed Qinling geology day on whatever routes are currently open; fitness and weather still come first. Qianling is for the surface plan and stone sculpture of a Tang imperial tomb, together with the distance from the city; settle the last leg before leaving. Choose one. The previous evening, check weather, opening notices, the group's energy and the return. If any one of those is unclear, use a city day instead.

p.src: Do not schedule another distant excursion on Day 5. First ask what the previous four days left behind. Return to Beilin if a late arrival removed it. Choose one smaller place if fatigue shortened a museum visit. If nothing important was missed, follow one new city thread. Daming Palace Archaeological Site extends the map of Tang Chang'an north from the pagoda district to the palace position on Longshouyuan, making it possible to reconsider the city's scale over half a day. Leave the other half for laundry, sleep, buying what the onward journey needs, or a meal without watching the clock. This margin can absorb changed weather, fatigue after a mountain day, or different energy levels between two travelers without forcing changes across the itinerary.

p.src: The same five days can change emphasis without adding more stops. First visit | Keep the base route: wall, Qin archaeology, the southern corridor and one nearby place. History-heavy | Enter Beilin on Day 1, give the basic museum display real time on Day 3, and use Daming Palace on Day 5; still choose only one excursion. Food-led | Keep the attraction count, lengthen dinner on Day 1 and lunch on Day 5, and use Chapter 6 to select a food setting already on that day's route. Family | Shorten the wall section, keep one indoor focus per half-day, and include toilet stops, seated rests and the hotel return. Reduced mobility | Verify each entrance, slope, lift, wheelchair service, drop-off and return segment. Accessibility inside one venue does not make the complete day step-free.

p.src: Fix only two meal positions each day: breakfast near the start and one proper meal near the final major stop. Roujiamo with liangpi can serve as the shorter meal. Give paomo, noodles or dumplings a seat and enough time when you want to pay attention to them. Eat in the old lanes on Day 1 and around Yanta on Day 3. On an excursion, accept that choices near the site may be limited, then decide whether to carry water and a small amount of food or eat after returning to the city. Do not cross Xi'an for one shop found online, and do not lose a reservation to a queue. Two travelers can each choose one dish and share one unfamiliar item. This makes it easier to remember what each person liked and reduces waste.

p.src: Use one city hotel for this route. Days 1 and 3 stay in the old core and south; Days 2 and 4 travel light from the same room, leaving Day 5 usable. Moving adds packing, checkout, luggage handling, a city transfer, another entrance and check-in; one shorter ride rarely repays that time. Split only for two consecutive Lintong days without a city return, or a final night near Xi'an North before a very early train. Otherwise, save the Chinese address, entrance and route back, and keep the room.

p.src: Obey closures, suspended services, severe-weather notices and on-site safety instructions. For a late start, queue or fatigue, protect the fixed booking and safe return, then keep the day's principal place. Cut the unbooked second interior first, then viewpoint detours, photo stops and a meal across town; shorten the principal visit last. Medication, water, a seat and a toilet are not cuts. Move a missed place to Day 5, or leave it for another trip. Do not carry delay into tomorrow or add a night stop to recover a daytime list.

p.src: Day 1, old core: South Gate, Beilin or Shuyuanmen, Bell and Drum Tower, then the lanes. Day 2, Qin archaeology: travel for the booked Lintong entry, read the three pits in sequence, and leave time for the return. Day 3, south: one museum, lunch and rest, then one pagoda; replace the morning if the booking fails. Day 4, choose one: Huashan, Han Yangling, Cuihuashan or Qianling. Day 5, return to the city: recover one missed place or follow one new thread such as Daming Palace. Each day has one principal place, one nearby group, one proper meal and margin for rest and return. Before leaving, recheck booking, opening status, weather, entrance and transport.
